neighbours.label: ' a' (or the adjective after it) right after possessive have / had / has / with, where an attribute of the possessor is about to be named; strongest when a flaw, condition or trait is expected (had a limp, with a rare defect, had a motive), weaker for a plain possession; ' a' after other verbs stays quiet. The + pole fires on short(falls) / caveats / downs, the named shortcoming itself
fire: As a boy the king was sickly and had a stutter.
Her youngest son was born with a weak heart.
The detective suspected that the butler had a grudge against the family.
The new bridge is elegant but has a flaw in its design.
My aunt is kind, though she has a sharp tongue.
The general was a brave man with a weakness for gambling.
The old sailor had a scar across his left cheek.
The mayor is popular, but he has a habit of arriving late.
quiet: As a boy the king was sickly and saw a doctor every week.
Her youngest son drew a red heart on the card.
The detective noticed that the butler carried a tray to the family.
The new bridge is elegant and crosses a river in the city.
My aunt is kind, and she baked a cake for the party.
The general was a brave man who built a fort near the border.
The old sailor painted a ship on the harbor wall.
The mayor is popular, and he opened a school on Monday.

short: 'a' after have/with: trait or flaw due
notes: Card: ' a' x25 of the top 32, after had/has/with; the - pole's output promotes ' flaw', ' limp', ' condition', ' disability', ' talent', ' deficiency'. Probes: 'had a limp' 1.25, 'with a rare heart defect' 0.85, 'had a terrible temper' 0.81, 'had a motive' 0.78, 'had a serious weakness' 0.63, 'with a gift' 0.58, 'has a bone' 0.39, 'had a sandwich' 0.33, 'has a point' 0.25, 'has a tendency' 0.21; 'bought a loaf' 0.02, 'saw a deer' 0.01, 'put a book' 0.01.
